title: Sharmila Dhankar Wins Para Athletics Gold at Commonwealth Games, Ending India's 20-Year Wait
excerpt: The 40-year-old from Haryana, who overcame polio and domestic violence to take up sport at 26, wins the women's shot put F57 at Glasgow 2026.
body:
• Sharmila Dhankar won gold in the women's shot put F57 at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, ending India's 20-year wait for a para athletics gold at the CWG.
  • The 40-year-old from Haryana contracted polio at age two, was thrown out of her marital home at 26 after years of domestic violence, and took up para athletics after her second husband sold their house to fund her training.
  • India's medal tally at Glasgow continues to grow, with the para contingent targeting five or more medals from an 11-member squad.
  • Teammate Shilpa KS also competed in the F57 shot put, giving India two athletes in the final.

A Gold 20 Years in the Making

Sharmila Dhankar stood over the throwing frame in Glasgow's Hampden Park and launched the shot that ended two decades of waiting. The 40-year-old from Chitrauli village in Haryana won gold in the women's shot put F57 at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, becoming the first Indian para athlete to win a CWG gold in athletics since the programme was introduced.

India has won eight para medals since para sports were included in the Commonwealth Games at Birmingham 2022, but a gold in athletics had remained elusive. Dhankar ended that drought with a performance that was as much about personal triumph as it was about sporting achievement.

From Chitrauli to Glasgow

Dhankar's journey to the top of the podium reads like a story that should not end with gold — and yet it does. Born to a poor farming family, she contracted polio at the age of two, losing the use of her legs. Married at 19, she endured years of domestic abuse as her husband harassed her over dowry demands. At 26, she was thrown out of her marital home along with her two daughters. Her parents took her back.

She remarried at 28. Her second husband, Ajit Singh, read about para athletics in a newspaper and encouraged her to try. To fund her training, he sold their house. It was, by any measure, a bet on the improbable.

Dhankar became a national champion in 2021. She represented India at the Birmingham Commonwealth Games in 2022 but finished a heartbreaking fourth. She placed fifth at the 2025 World Para Athletics Championships in New Delhi. Then came gold at the Fazza International Para Athletics Championship in Dubai earlier this year — and now, the biggest prize of all in Glasgow.

"She is an inspiration for proving that determination can overcome age and adversity."

— Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Sharmila Dhankar

India's Para Contingent Delivers

Dhankar's gold caps a strong showing from India's 28-member para contingent in Glasgow. The Paralympic Committee of India had targeted five or more medals, with PCI president Devendra Jhajharia expressing optimism about reaching seven or eight.

In the F57 shot put, India had the rare advantage of fielding two athletes. Shilpa KS, a 27-year-old from Karnataka who took up the sport after being inspired by a coach, also competed in the final. The pair had trained together and pushed each other through domestic competitions, with Dhankar winning gold at the Indian Open Para Athletics Championships in May with a throw of 9.86 metres, ahead of Shilpa's 6.67 metres.

The F57 classification covers athletes with lower-limb impairments or limb deficiencies who compete in seated throwing events using a specially designed frame. It demands explosive upper-body power and precise technique — qualities Dhankar has refined over years of training on modest resources.

What's Next

India's para athletics campaign at Glasgow continues with events across multiple disciplines. For Dhankar, the gold medal is validation of a journey that began in a village with no facilities, no infrastructure, and no precedent. At 40, she has no plans to stop. Her next target: the 2028 Paralympic Games in Los Angeles, where the F57 shot put will carry an even larger stage and a global audience.
